messages:
jen: heads up — seeing a jump in Xid 31 across rack r14 (us-west2). ~12 events in last 10m, concentrated on node-14/gpu-07 and node-18/gpu-02

mike: link to the graph?

jen: https://grafana.redwood/d/gpu/xid-spikes?panel=7 — spike starts ~12:02 UTC and is very bursty

jen: kernel logs show repeated 'NVRM: Xid (31): PTE page fault' interleaved with pcie/NET messages

sara: ran a quick tenant correlation — 7/12 of the Xid hits map to tenant `tts-batch` (low-latency small-decode workload)

sara: query snippet: `SELECT tenant, count(*) FROM gpu_errors WHERE xid=31 AND ts>now()-15m GROUP BY tenant` => tts-batch=7, rerank-prod=3, misc=2

chao: interesting — small batch (batch_size=1) decoders + frequent KV cache churn can amplify PCIe traffic. NVLink retransmits + pcie errors could surface as Xid31

mike: any recent driver/kernel/firmware pushes to that node group? timeline match would be useful

jen: yes — a kernel module push landed ~5m before the first spike on that node group (5.10.186 -> 5.10.188). also infra auto-updated nvidia driver on a subset earlier today

ops-sre: infra-bot created incident INC-7892 and paged on-call

infra-bot: [automated] incident INC-7892 created — GPU Xid 31 burst on r14 (us-west2). See: https://incidents.redwood/7892

sara: also seeing uptick in `pcie_uncorr_ecc` and `pci_retry` counters on gpu-07 in the same window

jen: logs (copied):
```
Mar 18 12:03:02 node-14 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): PTE page fault: GPU 00000000:03:00.0, pid 2241
Mar 18 12:03:02 node-14 kernel: pciehp 0000:03:00.0: Link Down
Mar 18 12:03:02 node-14 kernel: nv_peer_mem: device stuck, retrying
Mar 18 12:03:03 node-14 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): PTE page fault: GPU 00000000:03:00.0, pid 2250
```

chao: could be a flaky card (intermittent link flaps) or a driver regression that makes retries fatal. recommend: soft-drain the affected GPU, run memtest + firmware/BIOS rollback if memtest shows issues

mike: soft-drain impact? we lose 2 effective slots in us-west2 for ~30-45m while we test/replace — that might push some SLAs for latency-sensitive tenants

ops-sre: we can route critical traffic to the dedicated pool and divert non-critical to other regions; will coordinate with CS for affected customers

sara: short-term mitigation: throttle tts-batch to increase batching (batch_size -> 8) and reduce small-batch churn. That reduces packet bursts and KV cache thrashing

jen: creating a short playbook: 1) soft-drain node-14/gpu-07, 2) run gpu-memtest + nvdiag, 3) if memtest fails open HW RMA ticket, 4) if memtest clean, rollback driver on that host to previous version, monitor for recurrence

jen: playbook commands I'll run: `sudo /usr/local/bin/soft-drain node-14 --gpu 07` then `nvdiag --memtest --stress 30m`

infra-bot: command executed: `/cmd soft-drain node-14 --gpu 07` — queued on scheduler (job id: 43821)

chao: starting memtest now on node-14 (kickoff 12:12 UTC). will post results in this thread

mike: one thought — if driver push triggered this and memtest is clean, we should avoid fleet-wide rollback (expensive). prefer targeted drain + vendor escalation for that card's telemetry

jen: agreed. i'm opening a hardware follow-up ticket and attaching kernel/pcie counters + countersd dumps

jen: followups assigned: @chao run memtest + nvdiag, @mike check spare inventory and RMA process, @sara throttle tts-batch routes, @ops-sre coordinate routing and CS comms

sara: quick cost note: soft-drain + inter-region routing for 1h estimated +3% core infra cost for the hour (rough calc)

ops-sre: noted. we'll hold off on broad driver rollback until memtest/firmware checks complete

chao: memtest log (first 5m): `no ECC failures observed, some link resets during stress, nvlink_retries=13` — continuing to 30m

jen: thanks — if link resets continue, escalate to hardware vendor for board-level diagnostics. I'll update the incident with memtest output

mike: if vendor recommends replacement, plan change window next weekday morning (low load) to swap GPU module — need approval from finance for spare part cost if out of warranty

jen: filing replacement ticket now and adding impact estimate. will post final status when memtest finishes

ops-sre: please keep updates concise here. paging CS if replacement likely. :bell:

jen: update in 20m — memtest will finish around 12:42 UTC

sara: meanwhile I've throttled tts-batch routing and bumped recommended batch_size in the routing config. should see reduced bursts in the next 10-15m

jen: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
